project: Shifa International School — Website & Admin Panel
authority: This file is the ONLY place task status lives. BUILD-TRACKER.md defines tasks; it never records status.

status_values.todo: Not started. Eligible for selection when every `needs` id is `done`.
status_values.in_progress: Claimed by the current session. Only one task may hold this at a time.
status_values.done: Completed and verified. Its Verify commands passed.
status_values.blocked: Cannot be completed as written. `blocked_reason` is filled and the id is listed in `blocked_on`.
status_values.awaiting_human: Work an AI may not complete. Only a human may move this to `done`. Treated as NOT satisfying a dependency.
status_values.superseded: Replaced by a later task id. Never selected. Its output is not edited.

read_order_for_ai: 1. Read build-state.json only. Do not read SESSION-LOG.md or ARCHITECTURE.md yet.
2. Check blocked_on. If non-empty, STOP and report to the user.
2b. Check `phase_gates`. If a gate's condition is not met, no task it guards may be selected. A gate that guards ANY task in a batch blocks the ENTIRE batch, even the tasks it does not name.

3. Select the session's BATCH: the first entry in `batches` that still holds at least one 'todo' task and whose every external need is 'done'. An external need is any id in the `needs` of its tasks that is not itself a member of that batch; needs internal to the batch are satisfied by building in the batch's listed order. A need with status 'awaiting_human', 'blocked' or 'superseded' does NOT count as satisfied. That batch is the ONLY scope for this session. If no batch qualifies and at least one task is 'awaiting_human', STOP and report: 'Build is waiting on human sign-off for <ids>. A human must set these to done in build-state.json before work continues.'
4. Open BUILD-TRACKER.md ONCE and read the cards for every 'todo' task in the batch, in a single pass. Nothing else.

5. Open ARCHITECTURE.md ONCE and read the UNION of those cards' `Load` lines, deduplicated, in a single pass. Nothing else. Never re-open a section already read this session — this deduplication is the entire point of batching.

6. Build the batch's tasks in their listed order. For EACH task in turn: build exactly that card's Do list, touch only that card's Files, run that card's Verify commands until all pass, then commit 'T-0XX: <title>'. Then move to the next task WITHOUT re-reading build-state.json, BUILD-TRACKER.md or ARCHITECTURE.md.

7. If a task's Verify cannot be made to pass, or it turns out unbuildable as written: set THAT task to 'blocked', fill blocked_reason, add it to blocked_on, and STOP. Tasks already committed earlier in the batch keep their 'done' status; the untouched remainder stays 'todo' and becomes the next session's batch.

8. Update build-state.json ONCE, at the batch boundary: set every task completed this session to 'done', bump updated_at and updated_by (use the last completed id), correct `progress.done`, and set `done` to true for any milestone whose every task is now 'done'. Append ONE entry to SESSION-LOG.md (a separate file) covering the whole batch, with a short subsection per task — do not add it back into build-state.json.
9. STOP at the batch boundary. Do not begin the next batch, even if it looks trivial.
global_rules: ONE batch per session. Never cross a batch boundary. Batching shares the READING across a batch's tasks; it never shares their verification. Each task inside a batch still runs its own Verify to completion and still lands as its own commit, so any single module can be reverted without touching its neighbours.

A batch is a context budget, not a quota. If the remaining work will not fit in this session, finish the task in hand, write state per read_order step 8, and STOP mid-batch — an honestly short session is correct, a task compressed to fit is not. NEVER trim a card's Do list, skip a Verify, or merge two tasks' commits in order to reach the end of a batch.

Within a batch, a task may touch only its OWN card's Files — never an earlier task's output, which is still a revision under the rule below. Where two cards' Files globs overlap (e.g. T-051's `src/components/admin/**` contains T-052's `Dashboard*.tsx`), a file belongs to the task whose card names it most specifically, and the broader task must not pre-create it.

Never revise a 'done' task's work. If a done task's output is wrong, add a new task with a new id and set the old one's status to 'superseded'. Additively extending a shared file (adding a script to package.json, adding a job to ci.yml, appending a section to docs/RUNBOOK.md) is NOT a revision and is allowed when that path appears in the current card's Files list.
Never invent facts about the school. See ARCHITECTURE.md A-3.1. Use the literal marker [[CONTENT REQUIRED — DO NOT PUBLISH]].
If a task cannot be completed as written, set status 'blocked', fill blocked_reason, add to blocked_on, and STOP.
If the work would need files outside the card's Files list, STOP and report scope drift instead of expanding.
Every completed task = one commit, message 'T-0XX: <title>'.
PRODUCT-SPEC.md assumes every decision in ARCHITECTURE.md Parts A/B. If a task's Load line names both and they disagree, ARCHITECTURE.md wins.

build-state.json `needs` is the only authoritative dependency graph. A card's `Needs` and `Unlocks` lines are a human-readable mirror; if they disagree with the JSON, the JSON wins and the card must be corrected.

M8_before_launch.rule: No task in M9 or M10 may be selected until every M8 task is done.

human_gates.rule: T-131 is human-only. An AI sets it to 'awaiting_human' and never to 'done'. Only a human may set it to 'done', and that is what unblocks T-132.

ADR-005_route_shape.note: DECIDED. ADR-005's URLs are unchanged — `/notices` is Bangla, `/en/notices` is English, `/bn/*` is a 404. What changed is the App Router directory that implements them: a REQUIRED `[locale]` segment at `src/app/(public)/[locale]/`, with `src/middleware.ts` rewriting the bare Bangla namespace onto it (`/notices` -> `/bn/notices` internally, `/en/notices` passed through, an externally requested `/bn/*` rewritten to a non-locale segment so the layout's guard 404s it). The optional catch-all `[[...locale]]` the cards originally named is unusable: Next 15.5 throws `Catch-all must be the last part of the URL.` for EVERY request once any child route exists, and `next dev` will not start. Verified three ways in T-080's first session. The required segment also restores `generateStaticParams`, which the catch-all rejected (`Requested and resolved page mismatch: //notices /notices`), so §A-11's per-locale static generation is reachable again — T-103 owns wiring it. Applied 2026-08-17: the `Files` lines of T-080 and T-081..T-090 in BUILD-TRACKER.md now name `[locale]`, and T-080's `Files` line additively gains `src/middleware.ts` (the locale rewrite only — T-041's session and admin logic is untouched). No other done task was modified.

ADR-005_url_change.note: Bangla is unprefixed (/notices), English is /en-prefixed (/en/notices). Reverse only by a new ADR.

ADR-007_admin_language.note: Bilingual admin, per ARCHITECTURE A-18 ADR-007. Reverse only by a new ADR.

content_owners.note: A-3.1's 24 rows carry role owners, not named individuals. T-130 requires a named person and a deputy per row - see risk R9 (bus factor).

batching_policy.authority: `batches` is the only authoritative session-scope grouping. A task's membership lives here and nowhere else — task objects deliberately carry no batch field, so the two can never drift apart.
batching_policy.why: The per-session cost was never the building, it was the re-reading: every session re-opened this file, hunted one card in a 63KB BUILD-TRACKER.md, and re-entered a 138KB ARCHITECTURE.md for sections it had often already read. A batch pays that cost once and amortises it across tasks that share the same sections.
batching_policy.grouped_by: File-disjointness plus shared `Load` sections — NOT by milestone. A milestone is a reporting boundary; it is not evidence that its tasks are safe to build together.
batching_policy.sizing: 2-4 tasks where the pattern repeats and the reading overlaps. Never more: M5's twelve modules have no interdependencies at all and would batch cleanly on paper, but twelve modules of read model + UI + Server Actions + permission checks exceed one session's working context, and the failure mode is silent — cards get compressed to fit rather than the session stopping short.
batching_policy.always_solo: M8 (T-110..T-114) is the verification tier for everything M4-M7 built; batching a gate alongside more building lets the same session grade its own work. M10 (T-130..T-132) is irreversible — content load, human sign-off, DNS and credential rotation. T-104 and T-123 are solo for the same reason: one cross-cutting surface each, with no second task worth the risk of rushing it. Do not 'optimise' any of these into a batch later.
batching_policy.on_a_blocked_task: A batch is complete only when every task in it is 'done'. If one blocks, the batch ends at that task; the remainder stays 'todo' and is re-selected as the next session's batch.
